## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kosiyajātaka* (Ja 130) is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection, serving as the tenth and final story of the *Kusanāḷivagga* in the *Ekakanipāta* [Fausböll 1877]. The framing narrative is set at Jetavana concerning a woman of Sāvatthī, the deceitful wife of a devout and virtuous brahmin lay-follower; she was in the habit of roving about at night while feigning illness during the day to shirk household chores. In modern scholarship on the social attitudes of Buddhist narrative literature, the story is cited as an example of a recurring motif where brāhmaṇa wives are depicted as unchaste or corrupt [Goyal 2003].

In the conclusion to the story, the brahmin woman ceases her improper conduct out of reverence for the Buddha; the Master then connects the birth (*jātakaṁ samodhānesi*), declaring that the husband and wife were the same couple in their previous existence, while the Buddha himself was their wise teacher (*ācariyo*) [Fausböll 1877].
